findings.summary: getattr(target_sa, relation.back_populates) raises TypeError when back_populates is None for unidirectional relationships — a regression from the old code which used session.get() + session.refresh() and did not require back_populates
findings.failure_scenario: SQLAlchemy model defines orders: Mapped[list['Order']] = relationship() without back_populates. The auto-generated list resolver crashes with TypeError: getattr(): attribute name must be string because getattr(target_sa, None) is called.

findings.summary: The pagination query select(target_sa).join(back_attr).where(primary_col == entity_id) has no ORDER BY clause, making paginated results non-deterministic — items can appear on different pages or be missed across requests
findings.failure_scenario: A client calls page 1 (page_size=20) then page 2 on the same relationship resolver. Because the database returns rows in arbitrary order, item X appears on page 1 in the first call but also on page 2 in a subsequent call, or is entirely missed by both pages.

findings.summary: For self-referential one-to-many relationships (e.g. Employee.subordinates), where(primary_col == entity_id) filters by the target table's own PK instead of the FK, returning the wrong entity — the old session.get() + getattr() approach handled this correctly
findings.failure_scenario: Employee model with id, manager_id (FK to self), manager and subordinates relationships. Calling the subordinates resolver with entity_id=1 returns employee with id=1 (if they have a manager) instead of employees where manager_id=1.

findings.summary: The mutable_crud/app.py example was removed from the EXAMPLES smoke-test list, losing automated regression coverage for this example
findings.failure_scenario: A future change to EnrichMCP or EnrichModel breaks the mutable_crud example (e.g., removing a deprecated API it relies on). CI does not detect this because the example is no longer tested.
